assumptions: Canadian adult age-pooled, sex-specific smoking and heavy-alcohol marginals, not current Swiss age-specific prevalence.
Unknown joint exposure distribution: independent reference construction, not an empirically measured joint cohort.
Former-smoker reference quit time of 15 years is an explicit assumption, not a published mean.
Activity reference is the published median, not a full exposure distribution.

Synthetic diet score: male 2 + 3.3 - 2*(0.109 + 0.109 + 0.156) = 4.552; female 2 + 4.2 - 2*(0.096 + 0.086 + 0.116) = 5.604. Median fruit/veg frequency plus mean binary penalties; one excess juice frequency assumed when high. Not published mean diet scores.
Reference cigarette counts of 10 and 20 identify the published light/heavy bins; they are not observed mean cigarette counts.

adaptations: Only mutually adjusted behavioural coefficients are transported. Disease/social coefficients, the Canadian absolute hazard and age coefficient are not copied into the Swiss baseline. Unmeasured covariates are assumed common; this is not a validated full MPoRT implementation.
The observed moderate-alcohol association is set to zero, so starting alcohol never earns a bonus.
MPoRT BMI spline is not added. Our separate experimental SBMI correction replaces it; BMI-related residual confounding and mediation remain uncertain.
Activity is approximated from moderate/vigorous weekly minutes, not the complete Canadian activity questionnaire.
Expected years use annual hazard integration and a common published age-99 tail, normalized to the official starting E(x).
Smart BMI reduces modeled remaining years by a fraction of official remaining years, without an extra age multiplier. A hazard multiplier is solved to make the modeled curve agree with that target.
Apart from time since quitting smoking, behaviour is held constant into the future. No individual disease, treatment or weight trajectories are forecast.

The historical age factor is applied once to the joint lifestyle deviation by mixing personal and reference survival curves: 100% up to age 50, then (100-startingAge)/50. The same mixture is used in years and curves. This is an experimental adaptation, not an MPoRT coefficient or validated age interaction. Smart BMI is applied afterwards without that factor. Historical +12-year caps and remaining-years floors are not imported.

The simplified public form asks only total whole fruit/vegetable intake, including raw and cooked vegetables but excluding juice/fries/chips. Unasked carrot/potato/juice details are held at the same sex-specific Canadian Application reference means for everyone (Table 2/3; one excess juice occasion assumed in the high-juice subgroup, as in the existing reference). This is an explicit mean-score approximation, not observed personal answers or a validated substitute questionnaire. Legacy detailed profiles remain available for research comparison only.

The graphical public input now asks daily handful-sized portions. Portion counts are used one-for-one as a proxy for the previous frequency input; no empirical unit conversion is available. Cards 0/1/3/5/7+ set 0/1/3/5/7; optional exact entry retains 0-12 with the existing score cap at 8. Seven-plus is a lower-bound input category, not a recommendation or an extra bonus. The Swiss five-portions guideline explains portion size, not mortality coefficients.

The public alcohol input offers weekly bands 0, 1-14, 15-21 and 22+ or an exact count. Bands align with both existing sex-specific high-consumption thresholds; no range is treated as an invented exact number. The five-plus/binge response remains separate and is never inferred from a zero-drinks week. Coefficients and risk classification are unchanged.

lifestyleDiscount.source: Historical gesundheit.inc:550; linear age factor. Application to survival curves is our experimental adaptation.

dietInput.topCardMeans: 7 or more, modeled as 7 unless exact value entered
dietInput.mapping: one-for-one proxy, not a validated conversion
